title: The Box That Traveled Twice
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の教材例。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A fictional international youth organization invited schools to exchange boxes containing objects that represented their everyday lives.
sentences.ja: 架空の国際青少年団体は日常生活を表す品物を入れた箱を学校同士で交換するよう招いた。

sentences.en: One group carefully selected traditional crafts, photographs, and examples of the stationery used in its classrooms.
sentences.ja: 一つのグループは伝統工芸、写真、教室で使う文房具の例を慎重に選んだ。

sentences.en: The students assumed that their partners would immediately understand why each object had been included.
sentences.ja: 相手が各品を入れた理由をすぐ理解すると想定した。

sentences.en: However, several responses from the receiving school focused on details that the senders had considered unimportant.
sentences.ja: しかし受取校の反応のいくつかは送り手が重要でないと思った詳細に注目した。

sentences.en: A photograph of a classroom generated questions about the arrangement of the desks rather than the decorations on the walls.
sentences.ja: 教室写真は壁の装飾より机の配置についての問いを生んだ。

sentences.en: An ordinary notebook attracted more attention than a costly craft because the recipients recognized similarities with their own school materials.
sentences.ja: 普通のノートは自校教材との類似性が認められたため高価な工芸品より注目を集めた。

sentences.en: The students discovered that the significance of an object could depend on the experiences and interests of the person examining it.
sentences.ja: 物の重要性は見る人の経験や関心にも依存し得ると知った。

sentences.en: They therefore decided to exchange explanations of their questions as well as explanations of the objects themselves.
sentences.ja: そこで物自体の説明だけでなく質問の背景も交換することにした。

sentences.en: For the second exchange, each school included a short account of how a particular object was actually used.
sentences.ja: 二度目の交換で各校は特定の物の実際の使い方について短い説明を添えた。

sentences.en: They avoided claiming that a practice observed in one classroom was necessarily representative of an entire country.
sentences.ja: 一教室の慣行が必ず国全体を代表すると主張しなかった。

sentences.en: They also invited their partners to identify similarities and differences without ranking the objects according to their cultural importance.
sentences.ja: 文化的重要性で品物を順位づけせず類似と相違を見つけるよう求めた。

sentences.en: The resulting conversation encouraged both groups to examine aspects of their own surroundings that they had previously taken for granted.
sentences.ja: 会話は双方が以前当然視した自分の周囲の側面を調べるきっかけになった。

sentences.en: The organizers recognized that a small exchange could not establish accurate generalizations about national customs.
sentences.ja: 小規模交流では国の慣習について正確な一般化を確立できないと主催者は認識した。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the project provided an opportunity to discover questions that a conventional presentation might not have addressed.
sentences.ja: それでも従来型発表では扱わなかったかもしれない問いを発見する機会になった。

sentences.en: The students prepared a joint exhibition in which the objects appeared alongside questions and responses from both participating schools.
sentences.ja: 両校の質問と回答を品物と並べた共同展示を準備した。

sentences.en: They described the display as a record of a particular encounter rather than a comprehensive account of either country's culture.
sentences.ja: どちらかの国の文化の包括的説明でなく特定の出会いの記録と説明した。

sentences.en: Cultural exchange can become richer when participants are permitted to ask unexpected questions rather than merely receive information chosen for them.
sentences.ja: 用意された情報を受け取るだけでなく予想外の質問が許されると文化交流は豊かになり得る。

sentences.en: An ordinary object may reveal meaningful differences precisely because its original owner regards it as familiar.
sentences.ja: 普通の物は元の持ち主が身近と感じるからこそ意味ある違いを明らかにする場合がある。

sentences.en: The value of the exchange lies partly in the opportunity to reconsider what seemed too ordinary to explain.
sentences.ja: 交流の価値の一部は説明するほどでもないと思われたことを再考する機会にある。

sentences.en: Understanding another community may begin with noticing one's own daily life through the questions of someone else.
sentences.ja: 他者の共同体の理解は他者の問いを通して自分の日常に気づくことから始まり得る。
